### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**52** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ebfadb02c3a06153ff05af1cb620dfdc29bb6157`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **56** of **208** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ebfadb02c3a06153ff05af1cb620dfdc29bb6157` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `feca2c4fa92178393132e13ed9bb967886ead711` — the merge of head `7ad4554c39a4142810ebdcfab462967d638d6e49` into base `ebfadb02c3a06153ff05af1cb620dfdc29bb6157`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin feca2c4fa92178393132e13ed9bb967886ead711 && git checkout feca2c4fa92178393132e13ed9bb967886ead711
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ebfadb02c3a06153ff05af1cb620dfdc29bb6157 7ad4554c39a4142810ebdcfab462967d638d6e49 && git checkout -B drift-repro ebfadb02c3a06153ff05af1cb620dfdc29bb6157 && git merge --no-ff 7ad4554c39a4142810ebdcfab462967d638d6e49

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ebfadb02c3a06153ff05af1cb620dfdc29bb6157
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ebfadb02c3a06153ff05af1cb620dfdc29bb6157` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3e26252e655f21fb2e990efc111c16e383e38774`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-exchange-rate.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/plugin.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/plugin.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-lifecycle-health.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-object-references.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-nav-access.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts

Governing shape: ADR-0144 (PR #27239, head `775d8c09`, not yet on `main`) D3, D7 and Open items 7 and 11; ruling 6465431966 (#27119) and ruling 6469382727 (#27185: rate column decimal scale 12, total precision 24, never float). The tree was judged, not the PR body; where the two differ it is said below.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Registry entry** — `sys_exchange_rate` added to `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']`, sorted between `sys_email_template` and `sys_identity_email`. RIGHT, and forced: the spec ratchet (`platform-object-names.test.ts`) scans every `packages/**/*.object.ts`, derives the owner from the path segment before `src` (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-exchange-rate.object.ts` → `platform-objects`) and asserts set equality per group; without this hunk the ratchet reds on the new object file.
- **Accept-set widening at lint** — `isPlatformProvidedObjectName('sys_exchange_rate')` now answers true, so a stack reference to it is admitted at rung ③ (`validate-object-references.ts:238`, `validate-translation-references.ts:1848`, `stack.zod.ts:4581` action `objectName`) and `validate-nav-access.ts:162` skips the grant check for a nav item naming it ("granted by its own package"). RIGHT: `PlatformObjectsPlugin` registers the object unconditionally in its first manifest (`plugin.ts:198`, pinned by `plugin.test.ts`), so what lint admits resolves at runtime wherever `platform-objects` composes; the nav skip is right because the object's own grant is the `organization_admin` wildcard (not `access.default: 'private'`, no `requiredPermissions`), the same posture as the other object-type entries in `group_configuration`.
- **Runtime consumer** — `engine-lifecycle-health.ts#resolvePrimaryDatasource` iterates `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES`; `sys_exchange_rate` now votes as a witness when registered. RIGHT: it declares no `lifecycle.class` (not a system-ledger object) and rides the first manifest with no routing triple exactly like `sys_migration` / `sys_migration_journal` / `sys_secret`, so it lands on their datasource and cannot by itself produce `system-objects-split`.
- **`@objectstack/cli` inventory** — `organization-ownership-inventory.test.ts:123` requires a row for every registered name; the diff adds `sys_exchange_rate` (census `PMAIN`, fate `attribution`, no anchors). RIGHT; the `cli` patch in the changeset follows from it.
- **Tenancy census** — `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json` 87→88 registered, 44→45 in reach, `tenantField: organization_id`. RIGHT, derived artefact consistent with the hunk and with the object's no-opt-out tenancy.
- **Cloud repo at the next pin move** — `service-cloud` `control-plane-fate-supplement.test.ts` filters its supplement against the platform set (an added name changes nothing) and `objectos-runtime` `tenant-v18-upgrade-retired-tables.test.ts` only asserts retired names are absent. RIGHT: additive, neither breaks.
- **No new spec export** — `api-surface/system.json` and `export-origins/system.json` unchanged; `dangling-reference-audit.ts` reads only the `plugin-security` group. RIGHT, unaffected.
- **Published surface outside hits (lane's ACCEPT)** — `@objectstack/platform-objects` gains `SysExchangeRate`, `EXCHANGE_RATE_DIRECTION`, `EXCHANGE_RATE_SCALE`, `EXCHANGE_RATE_PRECISION` (`system/index.ts`), a Setup nav entry and four locales. Read for ②, not reviewed here.
- Wrong: none found in the hits hunk.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/27185-exchange-rate-table.md`: `@objectstack/platform-objects: patch`, `@objectstack/spec: patch`, `@objectstack/cli: patch`; body carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. Those three packages are exactly the released packages the diff moves (spec: registry membership; cli: inventory row; platform-objects: the object and its exports).
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: `sys_exchange_rate` is a system object an author cannot write (ADR-0029 D4), no authorable key, value or type changes. AGENTS.md Post-Task #3: "`none` takes `patch`" — so `patch` on all three is the rule's level. Precedent in `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` is split (17.2.0 `sys_flow_dispatch` under Patch Changes; 17.7.0 `sys_flow_credential` and `sys_comment_reaction` under Minor), the written rule governs. `Clause-②: no` matches the card's own declaration (`Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`) and appears line-initial in both PR body and changeset. Clause-②: no — matches the diff.
- The PR body's "Changeset: `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch" names one of the three bumps; the changeset itself is complete. Body correction only (③).

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` — nothing to answer.
- Out-of-scope finding 1 (#27192 writes amount × rate): ANSWERED by ADR-0144 D7 ("the home amount is the record amount divided by `rate`… #27192 follows parameter 3"). Nothing owed here.
- Out-of-scope finding 2 (parameter 4 unit): ANSWERED by ruling 6469382727 and APPLIED in the tree at `c8d84fd70`: `EXCHANGE_RATE_SCALE = 12`, `EXCHANGE_RATE_PRECISION = 24`, `rate` is `Field.number` with `scale: 12`, `precision: 24`, `min: 1e-12`; `FieldSchema` carries both keys (`field.zod.ts:1335`, `:1359`, ceiling `MAX_RENDERABLE_SCALE = 100`) and the write seam refuses by rejection, never rounding (`record-validator.ts` `max_scale` / `max_precision`). ⚠️ The PR body still says `scale: 18`, "Why 18, not 12", and "settling the open item later edits `EXCHANGE_RATE_SCALE`" — stale against the tree. ESCALATED to the dev: correct the body. Should-fix (account, not tree).
- Out-of-scope finding 3 (behavioural admin-201 / member-403 / duplicate-409 / cross-org-201 NOT MEASURED, carrier #27197): accepted as stated; the declaration each mechanism reads is pinned on the built value in `sys-exchange-rate.object.test.ts`.
- Out-of-scope finding 4 (file-surface breach: census artefact): declared. ⚠️ Two further breaches are UNDECLARED: `packages/spec` (`4bc2a793a`) and `packages/cli` (`c9ba0b689`, `3e26252e6`) landed after the os-dev-report, and the PR body's Human Minimum #1 "(No spec change.)" and #6 "`packages/spec` not touched" are false against the tree. Both edits are legitimate and forced (the spec ratchet and the cli inventory test red without them), so this is a body-account defect: ESCALATED to the dev to correct #1/#6 and name the breach. Should-fix.
- ADR-0144 Open item 11 (owner package, against ADR-0029 D1/D3/D6 and ADR-0028): SETTLED IN THE TREE by placement under `platform-objects` with the rationale in `plugin.ts` (its one reader is the engine's write path, present in every composition that can write a record; registered with the engine-facing infrastructure, like `sys_migration` / `sys_secret`). Defensible under ADR-0029 D2 (no on/off capability boundary) even though D6 wants `platform-objects` to shrink; ADR-0144's own M1-1 row names this package. NOT STATED in the PR body or on the card, and ADR-0144 says it is amended with each answer. ESCALATED: the dev states the ADR-0029 settlement on the card so #27239 can amend Open item 11. Should-fix.
- **Gate verdicts: PENDING.** `check-runs` on `3e26252e…`: `total_count: 0`; `check-suites`: 5 queued (`vercel`, `fly-io`, `claude`, `cloudflare-workers-and-pages`, `objectstack-fleet`), none concluded; commit status `pending`. The lane's local dispatch-gates run was on `faf1b6e3` / `86e39faf0`, not this head. No derived gate is adopted as green here; the queue guard stays whole-PR.
- **Merge state: `mergeable: false` (`dirty`).** `content/docs/ui/setup-app.mdx` was deleted on `main` by #27179 (`1287b2fa30`, 2026-10-28; its Setup-group anchors moved to `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx`, the `group_configuration` row near line 800) while this PR edits it: the docs hunk would resurrect a retired page and cannot merge. Outside `hits` (lane's ACCEPT), ESCALATED to the lane seat: rebase onto `main` and move the Exchange Rates row and the "how finance records a month's rates" entry into `ui/apps.mdx`. Blocks landing; not a contract-face defect.
- Release pairing: body carries "⛔ not released alone — pairs with #27192 (R2)"; PR is a draft. Consistent with the claim and ADR-0144 D9.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts` (schema face: the curated platform object registry, read by lint, the engine and the cli).

- **Against the code it cites.** The file's own maintenance contract ("adding an object to a platform package means adding its name here; the owning package's conformance test fails otherwise") is enforced by `platform-object-names.test.ts`, which derives the owning group from the file path and compares sets. The hunk adds the one name that test now finds in `packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-exchange-rate.object.ts` (`ObjectSchema.create({ name: 'sys_exchange_rate' … })`), under the group that path yields, in sorted position. HOLDS.
- **Against its first consumer (lint rung ③ and the nav-access skip).** Tried to break it: (i) a composition without `platform-objects` — then every name in that group is equally absent, which is the registry's stated contract ("registered by a package in this repo"), identical to `sys_user`; (ii) a composition with `platform-objects` — the object registers unconditionally in the first manifest, so a lint-admitted reference resolves; (iii) the engine's primary-datasource vote — the new witness lands with its three manifest siblings; (iv) the cloud repo's two registry readers — additive and tolerant. No reader is made wrong by the entry. HOLDS.
- **Against the ADR it implements (ADR-0144 D3, Open items 7 and 11).** D3 names `sys_exchange_rate { currency, rate, effective_date, source }` as a platform system object; the registry names it under the package ADR-0144's M1-1 row and the epic territory name. Open item 7 (uniqueness and audit) is answered in the object the entry points at: one unique key `(currency, effective_date)` spelled `unique: 'organization'` (ADR-0120 D1), `trackHistory` on object and the four columns, not on plugin-audit's skip list. Open item 11 is answered by placement, see ③. HOLDS; the settlement wants writing down (should-fix, ③).
- **Against ruling 6469382727.** The hits file carries no numeric claim; the object it names declares `number` / `scale 12` / `precision 24` / `min 1e-12`, and the engine refuses rather than rounds at both seams. The PR body's `scale 18` account is the only disagreement, and it is the body that is wrong. HOLDS.
- **Must-fix:** none.
- **Should-fix:** (1) PR body stale against the tree — `scale 18` → `scale 12 / precision 24`, Human Minimum #1/#6 and the changeset line must name the `packages/spec` and `packages/cli` edits; (2) the ADR-0029 D1/D3/D6 ownership settlement is stated nowhere the ADR can read it — state it on the card so #27239 amends Open item 11; (3) [lane seat] the `setup-app.mdx` hunk conflicts with `main`'s deletion of that page — rebase and move the docs line to `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx`.
